correctness.rationale: In bipartition U,V of Q_d, each with N=2^{d-1}, the nonconstant singular norm of incidence operator T is d-2 for d>=3, from Walsh levels. For endpoints A subset U and B subset V of an induced matching of size k, edges between A and B number exactly k, so k >= d k^2/N -(d-2)k(1-k/N), hence k<=N/2=2^{d-2}. The coordinate/parity families attain bound. At equality, centered ±1 indicator F lies in span of d coordinate Walsh characters on U, and G uses the opposite coefficients on V. Hence linear L(z)=sum c_i z_i has L(z)^2=1 for every z in {±1}^d; its Fourier coefficients imply c_i c_j=0 for all i!=j, so one coefficient ±1 and only the 2d canonical maximum matchings exist. Their edge partition forces unique optimum 2d-color strong edge coloring; exchange graph has isolated vertices for d>=3. d=2 has four singleton maxima and complete exchange graph. Independent exhaustive enumeration checked dimensions 2,3,4, separately from infinite proof.
